_comment: Budgets and conventions per kind of texture. A game's manifest may override any value or add profiles under "profiles", and one texture may override values under "overrides". Sizes are texels; colour distances, contrasts and steps are 8-bit levels (0 to 255); shares are 0 to 1. What a texture is used as (base colour, normal map, emissive) is not the profile's business: it is read from the glTF material that samples it, else from the name's ending (role_suffixes), else "role".

default._comment: Anything else. Also holds every threshold the other profiles inherit.
default._how_it_is_sampled: filter: how the game magnifies it (nearest, linear, any); a glTF sampler overrides it for that material. tile: which way it repeats (none, u, v, both). mips: whether the engine builds a mip chain for it (world textures and backdrops: yes; canvas images: no).
default._file: lossless: JPEG is not acceptable. A PNG is bloated when it is over bloat_ratio times the size of the smallest plain PNG of the same pixels and the difference is over bloat_min_bytes. max_metadata_bytes: text, time stamps, EXIF.
default._alpha: alpha: the most transparency the profile expects (none, mask: 0 or 255 only, blend). alpha_data: straight (what the engine's alpha blend and canvas expect) or premultiplied. margin: texels of clear border the content must leave (per cell, when `cell` [w, h] is set). A fringe is a fully transparent texel that touches one of at least fringe_alpha and holds a colour more than fringe_distance from it.
default._colour: min_peak: the 99th percentile of luminance must reach this (else crushed). max_floor: the 1st percentile must be under this (else blown). min_contrast: the 5th-to-95th percentile span. Pixel art: max_colours; a colour within near_colour_distance of a more used one is a near duplicate, and more than max(near_colour_min, near_colour_share of all colours) of them is a cloud. palette_tolerance: how far a colour may be from the game's palette.
default._tiling: A seam: the step across the wrap is over seam_factor times the largest step between neighbours inside (and over seam_min levels), texel to texel or between eighths of the image. repeat_contrast: how far one sixteenth of a tile may stand from the typical one. Shimmer: over shimmer_share of the contrast (and shimmer_min levels) is single-texel detail. atlas_max_empty: the share of an atlas that may be one flat colour, once that is more than atlas_min_waste texels.
default._ready: pot: sides must be powers of two. max_megabytes: RGBA8 on the GPU, a third more with mips.
default._normal_maps: normal_green: which way the engine reads a normal map's green channel: up the image, as glTF defines it, whether the mesh carries tangents or the engine derives them (engine/assets/Model.cpp, generateTangents). A map's own direction is trusted when it fits normal_green_confidence times better than the other.
default._emissive: A texel brighter than emissive_dark on any channel is lit; more than emissive_max_lit of the map lit is too much.
default._lut: The engine resamples every .cube to 16 cubed.

tile._comment: A tiling pixel-art world texture: a wall, a floor, rock. Repeats both ways, nearest filtering, mips, opaque.

trim._comment: A trim sheet: horizontal bands of pixel art (mouldings, pipes, plating, banners) that repeat along U only; a mesh picks a band with its V. May be cut out (mask).

atlas._comment: A texture painted for one model's unique UVs (a character, a boss, a prop, a floor medallion): pixel art, does not repeat. Padding between islands is modelkit's (UV) business.

overlay._comment: A see-through pixel-art layer on world geometry that repeats: mist, cobwebs, water foam, a decal strip. Blended, so soft alpha is expected.

normal_map._comment: A normal map that stands alone as a file (one a glTF material uses is recognised without this profile). Give it the layout of its colour map with overrides ("tile": "both").

emissive._comment: An emissive map that stands alone as a file (one a glTF material uses is recognised without this profile).

effect._comment: A soft image drawn additively or blended, scaled and filtered linearly: a glow, a light shaft, a vignette, a smoke puff that is not a sprite sheet. Needs a clear margin so it is not cut at its quad's edge.

ui._comment: Canvas art: panels, cursors, icons, button glyphs. The canvas draws images as they are stored (no sRGB decode, straight alpha, no mips, clamped), point sampled unless the call says linear = true; this profile assumes linear, as a smooth high-resolution UI uses (set "filter": "nearest" and "pixel_art": true for a pixel-art UI). Overrides: "nine_slice": the border the game passes to fe.canvas.nine_slice; "cell": [w, h] for a sheet of glyphs.

backdrop._comment: A sky card (environment.sky.backdrops) or a panorama: decoded from sRGB, filtered linearly, enlarged many times. Cards get mips and are clamped; a panorama wraps along U (override "tile": "u") and has no mips. Photographic panoramas may be JPEG (override "lossless": false).

lut._comment: A colour grade: a .cube 3D LUT named by a map's environment.post.lut. Not an image: checked as the table the engine builds from it.
